chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from al-Haytham ibn 'Urwah al-Tamimi who said:

A man asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihsar (state of consecration for Hajj/Umrah) who wishes to perfect his wudu (ablution), and a hair or two hairs fall from his beard, so he said: 'It is of no consequence. What God has placed upon you in the religion is not a hardship.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Does losing a few beard hairs during wudu invalidate the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-yusr* (ease) within Shia fiqh, distinguishing between intentional grooming and incidental hair loss during ritual purification. It reinforces the juristic view that minor, unavoidable shedding of beard hairs while washing does not break the state of ihram, reflecting the broader Quranic ethos that divine law avoids undue hardship for the believer.
